The analysis only sees code it compiles
The compiler reasons about your source code. Anything that creates objects at runtime, or was compiled without your annotations, is outside its view. That's where nulls get in:

content.text: By default, System.Text.Json treats every constructor parameter as optional and fills a missing one with its default value, which for a
is null. Since .NET 9, two opt-in options close that door:
for a non-nullable property or parameter, and
rejects a missing constructor parameter. Microsoft recommends both for new applications. The bad request now fails at the edge, with a message that names the field, instead of deep inside a service.
